podcast.title: Acquisitions of Independent Labels (1989)
podcast.body: Polygram acquired both Island Records and A&M Records in 1989. These acquisitions were significant in consolidating independent labels into larger corporate structures, eventually leading to Polygram morphing into Universal, one of today's three major labels. "Island was bought by Polygram in 1989, which eventually morphed into Universal, one of today's three major labels."

podcast.title: Role in Nirvana Single Release (1991)
podcast.body: Iver Hamilton, who had moved from a radio station to Polygram Records, was instrumental in bringing the CD single for Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" to a radio station for its initial play on August 27, 1991. "Iver Hamilton, who was working, who used to work at the radio station, had moved on to polygram records, came into the studio and he had the CD single and he says, put this on."

podcast.title: Signing Pulp (1992)
podcast.body: As part of a massive search for new artists after acquiring independent labels, Polygram found Pulp in 1992 and signed them to Island Records. "En 1992, durante ese proceso masivo de compra de artistas o de búsqueda de nuevos artistas, incluso de otras discográficas que había tenido después haber sido comprada por Polygram, encuentra el grupo de Pulp y lo consiguen meter en Island Records."

podcast.body: Iver Hamilton, a former colleague from the radio station who had moved to Polygram Records, brought the CD single of "Smells Like Teen Spirit" to the studio on August 27, 1991, instructing the speaker to play it. podcast.title: Acquisition of Independent Labels
podcast.body: Polygram, facing a crisis similar to Sony's in the early 1990s, initiated a process of acquiring several independent record labels. Among these, they bought two of the most important in the UK, including Island Records. "Polygram compró dos de las que posiblemente eran las discográficas independientes más importantes del Reino Unido entre ellas, Island Records."

srcs.episode: El BRIT POP como negocio discográfico

podcast.title: Major Label Adoption of "New Wave"
podcast.body: Polygram Records was one of the major labels that promptly adopted Seymour Stein's "New Wave" marketing term. This quick adoption, along with Warner Brothers Records and other major labels by 1980, was crucial in solidifying "New Wave" as a pervasive umbrella term for the varied new music coming out in the wake of punk. "Seymour's marketing term was then picked up by Warner Brothers Records, and then by Polygram Records, and then other major labels."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Significant Financial Investment in Pulp
podcast.body: To ensure the success of Pulp, a band that had little success over 10 years, Polygram made a substantial financial investment in them, allowing for high-profile production. "desembarcar económicamente por todo lo alto."
